monthly_readings.note: Baseline period — NWF intact, export revenue near pre-war levels with manageable discount

Jun 24: OFP initialized at 54. Export revenue proxy: seaborne exports down ~15% Jun vs May, Urals-Brent spread ~$13-15 (~score 55). NWF liquid portion ~2.5-3% of GDP, down from ~8% pre-war (~score 55). OFZ prices fell Jun 23-24, ruble past 75/dollar (~score 57). Regional cuts: national fiscal stress evident but no confirmed direct occupation transfer cuts yet (~score 48). Shadow fleet: ongoing but no acute new enforcement event (~score 35). OFP modulator applies +2 to MTCS (band: 41-55). Hormuz MOU (Jun 2026) ambiguous — Iranian supply return could soften Urals price realization; monitoring export revenue proxy for response. Sources: Reuters Jun 23, Minfin NWF disclosures, Kpler/Reuters export data. | Jul 17: OFP 54→58 (modulator +2→+4, entering 56–70 band). Behavioral signals confirming fiscal pressure on occupation-war funding stream: VTB reducing ATM withdrawal limits for Crimea customers; Russian federal government emergency subsidy of ₽4.3B to Crimea tourism companies (reactive fiscal expenditure confirming civilian economic collapse); ten canceled state fuel procurement tenders across Samara, Tambov, Stavropol — ambulances and utility services running on reserves (Izvestiya/Kyiv Post Jul 13); Russia importing gasoline from India (400,000 MT/month planned) and seeking jet fuel from Japan via multi-leg routing — import dependency deepening materially; Russian oil refining at lowest level since 2005 (Kyiv Post Jul 14). Deputy PM Novak publicly acknowledged national fuel crisis ‘due to [Ukrainian] strikes’ (Kyiv Post Jul 13). OFP modulator advances to +4 — occupation funding stream under meaningful strain. | Aug 9: OFP 58→70 (ceiling of 56–70 band; modulator holds at +4). Monthly anchor update from Minfin Aug 6 disclosure. NWF liquid assets 3.953T rubles ($48.3B) as of Aug 1, down from $52.6B Jul 1 — 1.8% of projected GDP vs ~8% pre-war. Gold holdings: 179.097 tonnes Aug 1 vs 405 tonnes pre-war — 71%+ depleted. Record daily gold/yuan sales pace from Jan 16 onward, exceeding Covid-era peak (12.8B rubles/day). 2026 budget projected zero NWF withdrawals; actual pace is record drawdown. Budget shortfall 4.6–5.5T rubles (Gazprombank/Polevoy estimates) against oil revenues running 1.1–3T rubles below target. OFZ market supported by CBR emissions — monetization of debt rather than market demand. Liquid assets heading toward 1% of GDP threshold on current trajectory; next crossing (OFP 71+) triggers modulator jump to +6. Sources: Minfin Aug 6 via Interfax/Investing.com, TASS Jul 3, Moscow Times Jan 2026, United24 Media Apr 2026, RANEPA/Gaidar Institute depletion analysis. | Aug 26: OFP 70→74; modulator advances +4→+6 (71–85 band). Threshold crossed on Minfin Jan–Jul budget execution (pub Aug 12): federal deficit 6.5T rubles / 2.8% of GDP against a full-year target of 3.8T — 1.7× the annual plan with five months to run; revenue 22.1T, spending 28.6T (+14.5% YoY); planned annual spending revised 44.1T→45.1T, projecting a full-year deficit near 4.8T. None of the three triggers named on Aug 9 (structural emissions-supported OFZ auctions, liquid assets below 1% GDP, missed occupation transfer payment) fired; the crossing is made deliberately on the deficit blowout as a fact of the same class — the outcome those triggers were proxies for. NWF component held at 72: no Minfin NWF disclosure this window, Aug 6 release (Aug 1 data) remains the anchor, next expected ~Sept 3. Export revenue proxy 62→72 on CREA July data (pub Aug 10): oil product loadings 4.7Mt, −23% MoM and lowest on record, under half July 2025’s 9.6Mt; product export revenue €116M/day −45% MoM; total fossil export revenue €683M/day −12% MoM; Urals $60.22 at 26% ($21) discount, price realisation ~0.74 vs 0.80 baseline. Bloomberg Aug 25: seaborne crude 3.46M bpd four-week average (four-month low, fifth consecutive weekly decline), gross export value $1.65bn/week (−$80M), crude output 8.89M bpd (six-year low, ~1M bpd below OPEC+ quota). Novorossiysk loadings ~400k bpd vs 800k–1,000k Jun/Jul; western-port exports 2.3M bpd vs 2.7M plan; zero crude loadings week ending Aug 16. OFZ 63→66 on the deficit and on VEB.RF chief economist Klepach’s dismissal (~Aug 18) after stating Russia ‘will not win’ the attrition war. Shadow fleet 42→52: Turkish Dardanelles transit restrictions (Aug 9), Skiros struck at CPC terminal Aug 16 ending the three-week lull, third-country-flagged RMS TEAM abandoned and VOLGO-BALT 226 damaged Aug 21, 36 vessels struck Aug 17–22, Kerch Strait blocked 30 consecutive days. Counter-signal logged and rejected as an anchor: a European intelligence source cited by Ukraine Business News (Aug 20) claims Urals averaged $82/bbl in Q2 adding ~$30bn in export revenue and fiscal runway to spring 2027 — this conflicts with CREA’s $60.22 July figure; CREA is the methodology’s named source for this component and the $82 figure is treated as a Q2 average at best, not an August anchor. Next watch: liquid assets below 1% GDP at the ~Sept 3 Minfin disclosure, or OFP above 85 (modulator +8). Sources: Minfin via Interfax/NV Aug 12, CREA monthly analysis Aug 10, Bloomberg Aug 25, Reuters Aug 17 and Aug 19, ISW Aug 19–23, Firstpost Aug 18. | Sep 9: OFP 74→76; modulator HOLDS at +6 (76 sits inside the same 71–85 band as 74), mtcs_base 78 and mtcs_final 84 unchanged. Nine-digest backlog 2026-08-27 → 2026-09-09. TWO INDEPENDENT ANCHORS, not one datum restated. (1) CBR data via Moscow Times / United24 (Aug 27): Russian energy exporters sold only $2.2bn in foreign currency on domestic markets in July — the lowest monthly volume in four years and a 3.5-fold drop from June — despite H1 2026 export revenue rising 15%; retention abroad attributed to asset-nationalisation fears; ruble down more than 20% since the start of summer. (2) KSE Institute August Chartbook (Sep 4): July export earnings $13.8bn, down from $15.8bn in June; export VOLUMES 7.0M bpd, down from 7.6M — a structural volume decline, not a price effect; OFZ issuance at its lowest since September 2022 with auctions suspended through at least September. DIGESTS 08-28 AND 08-29 CITE THE SAME CBR DATUM AND ARE ONE ANCHOR, NOT TWO. NWF TRIGGER REMAINS ARMED AND UNFIRED: the pre-registered advance from modulator +6 to +8 is conditioned on Minfin’s NWF liquid assets disclosure showing liquid assets below 1% of GDP. That disclosure was expected ~Sep 3 and is NOT VISIBLE IN ANY SOURCE as of this package — 6 days overdue and unobserved. Non-publication is not the trigger; the NWF component is held unchanged at 72 on the Aug 6 anchor. | MONTH KEY ROLLED 2026-06 → 2026-09 on 2026-09-09, David’s ruling, following the same roll on cities[*].history. NO SCORE MOVED IN THIS OPERATION — only the `month` key changed. The reason re-key rather than append: every reading before this one is `real: false`, a seeded backfill with no sources and no note, while this one is `real: true` and carries the dated log above running through September. It was never a June reading; it is the live entry, opened in June and maintained since, and the key now says so. Cadence: quarterly (2025-06, -09, -12, 2026-03, ...) — so 2026-09 is the NEXT SCHEDULED PERIOD for this series, not a skip.
monthly_readings.override_rationale: Stored OFP 74 carries a +7.45 judgment overlay above the weighted component computation (66.55). The overlay represents CBR emissions support for OFZ auctions - debt monetisation rather than market demand - which the five-component structure has no line item for and which the ofz_debt_stress component alone would overstate if forced to carry it. Overlay was +8.35 at the Aug 9 review and is narrowing as components catch up to the qualitative assessment. Reviewed and reaffirmed 2026-08-26.
